questions.questionText: What mechanism does LangGraph's human-in-the-loop interrupt rely on?
options: A completely separate system unrelated to anything else in LangGraph
The same checkpointing mechanism used for persistence — pausing before a node, saving state, and waiting to be explicitly resumed
A hardcoded delay before every tool call
A second LLM that approves or rejects actions automatically
questions.correctAnswer: The same checkpointing mechanism used for persistence — pausing before a node, saving state, and waiting to be explicitly resumed
questions.explanation: Interrupts build directly on checkpointing: since state is already saved after every step, LangGraph can pause before a chosen node and wait indefinitely for a resume call.

questions.questionText: Why is it a bad idea to interrupt before every single tool call, including harmless read-only ones?
options: It creates approval fatigue — users start rubber-stamping everything without really checking, defeating the purpose
LangGraph limits you to one interrupt per graph
questions.correctAnswer: It creates approval fatigue — users start rubber-stamping everything without really checking, defeating the purpose
questions.explanation: Interrupts are most valuable when reserved for actions with real consequences; overusing them trains users to approve without actually reviewing.

questions.questionText: How do you resume a graph that's paused at an interrupt, without providing new input?
options: You must restart the entire graph from the beginning
Call .invoke(null, { configurable: { thread_id } }) with the same thread_id — it continues from exactly where it paused
Interrupts cannot be resumed once triggered
You need to recompile the graph with a new checkpointer
questions.correctAnswer: Call .invoke(null, { configurable: { thread_id } }) with the same thread_id — it continues from exactly where it paused
questions.explanation: Passing null input with the matching thread_id tells LangGraph to continue the paused execution using its saved checkpoint state.
